With that file-storage background, let’s build the cache.
First, why do it? Mainly for user experience. Suppose someone browses Jianshu’s homepage and several detail pages, then wants to revisit them on the subway with poor or no connectivity. Saving those pages locally makes that experience comfortable. Previously viewed pages can load locally first, retrieving updates from the server only when needed, avoiding repeated waits.
My current app needs local storage on every page, and its chat images and audio need storage too.
Let’s build a convenient library for these cases.
Because this is cached data, I use the Caches folder. For management by category, I create separate subfolders. Page caches contain objects; images and audio each get their own folder. An enum manages these types and makes later additions easy.
